about.title: Dorris Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Dorris sits along Rt 97, a corridor that carries a mix of local traffic and through-travelers heading across Siskiyou County, and that mix shows up in the crash reports for streets like 1st Street, N Main Street, and 4th Street. Even a small town like Dorris sees collisions that leave people with real injuries and real bills, often on weekend nights when reported crashes tend to cluster between midnight and 2 a.m. on Fridays. We listen to what happened, evaluate your case, and explain your options under California law. We work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover. Whether the crash happened downtown or out on the highway, getting the right information early can matter for how your claim moves forward.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Dealing with Insurance

items.title: California's Two-Year Clock
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury lawsuit in California, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity was involved. We can help you figure out which deadline applies before it's too late.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work Against You
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning your compensation can be reduced by any percentage of blame assigned to you — even if you're only slightly at fault. Insurers often use recorded statements to shift blame your way, so it's worth speaking with us before giving one.

items.title: No Cap on Non-Economic Damages
items.desc: Unlike some states, California doesn't limit compensation for pain, suffering, and other non-economic losses in most car accident cases. We can help make sure those losses are properly documented and valued, not just your medical bills.

items.question: I was in a crash on Rt 97 near Dorris — what should I do first?
items.answer: Get medical attention even if you feel okay, since some injuries show up later. Try to document the scene, get contact info for any witnesses, and avoid giving a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer until you've talked to us. Contact us at no cost to discuss your claim.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Dorris?
items.answer: California generally gives you two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. That timeline can be much shorter — sometimes six months — if a government entity, like a public road agency, is involved. We can help pin down the exact deadline for your situation.

items.question: Does it cost anything to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: No. Your free case review costs nothing. We typically work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no upfront cost or obligation to see what your options might be.
